issues_detected.description: keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). It falls below the five-keyword expectation and, more importantly, covers only the domain: none of the disease cohorts (voice, neurological, mood/psychiatric, respiratory disorders), none of the acoustic methods (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory coding, phonetic posteriorgram) and none of the data modalities documented at length elsewhere in the record are reachable by keyword search.
issues_detected.recommendation: Expand keywords with the cohort conditions, the acoustic feature families, the collection modality (speech, cough, breathing) and the platform/standard terms (PhysioNet, BIDS) that already appear in description, instances and preprocessing_strategies.

issues_detected.description: No download_url slot is populated. Access is nevertheless operationally resolvable: the PhysioNet version-specific landing page, the registered-access procedure, the DACO review route and the Synapse controlled-access URLs are all given.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the PhysioNet files endpoint for v3.1.0 so machine clients can resolve the distribution without parsing prose.

issues_detected.description: distribution_formats names formats and even individual file names but records no media_type (MIME) and no character encoding for the TSV and JSON products.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add media_type (application/vnd.apache.parquet, text/tab-separated-values, application/json) and state UTF-8 encoding for the text products.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts states plainly that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk concedes that voice is inherently identifying and that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved. A formal DPIA is the instrument that would normally be expected given that admitted residual risk, even though the consortium substitutes an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access.
issues_detected.recommendation: Conduct and record a formal data protection impact assessment covering the feature-only release, or state explicitly why the published ethical-justification memorandum is held to discharge that function.

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements declares sensitive_elements_present: true for race/ethnic origin, sexual orientation and socioeconomic/health information, while the notes on the same block state that fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap data dictionary were removed before release along with household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences. A reader cannot determine from these two statements which sensitive attributes survive into the published feature-only release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Separate the attributes present in the published release from those removed during de-identification, ideally by scoping each sensitive_elements entry to the release it describes.

issues_detected.description: The RRID quoted in citation, RRID:SCR_007345, is well formed but identifies PhysioNet as a resource rather than this dataset. It is therefore a platform identifier carried into the citation string, not a persistent identifier for the Bridge2AI-Voice release; the identification burden is carried entirely by the DOI.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the DOI as the dataset identifier and label the PhysioNet RRID as a platform resource identifier to avoid the impression that the dataset itself carries an RRID.

issues_detected.description: is_tabular is not set although the release distributes tab-separated phenotype tables, static features and audio quality metrics alongside the Parquet tensors, and the variables block enumerates tabular columns.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set is_tabular to reflect the mixed tabular/array composition of the release, or state the mixture explicitly.

issues_detected.description: No structured imputation_protocols block is present. The substance is supplied instead by missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy, which states that no imputation is performed and that a missingness table accompanies the release, so the concept is documented even though the dedicated slot is empty.

semantic_insights: DOI prefix 10.13026 is the PhysioNet registrant prefix and is used consistently across id, doi, citation and every related_datasets PhysioNet target; the version-specific DOI and the version-independent concept DOI are correctly distinguished, with the latter placed in version_access.latest_version_doi rather than conflated with the release identifier.

Grant identifier OT2OD032720 parses correctly as NIH activity code OT2, institute code OD and serial 032720, and the supplement suffixes 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and -01S3 are well-formed NIH project numbers consistent with the stated Common Fund Bridge2AI program.

Participant arithmetic reconciles across three independent statements: collection_timeframes reports 306 + 136 + 391 cumulative additions, which sums to the 833 adult participants asserted in description and in instances.counts.

Temporal ordering is coherent: collection over roughly twelve months, releases from v1.0 (November 2024, Health Data Nexus) through v3.1.0 (1 May 2026, PhysioNet), with the issued date 2026-05-01 matching the v3.1.0 release date and the page URL pinned to /3.1.0/.

The de-identification strategy is semantically appropriate to the data type rather than boilerplate: it recognises that a waveform cannot be de-identified at all, states that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved, and responds by withholding raw audio entirely and releasing only derived features, with free-speech-derived dense features additionally excluded.

Human-subjects logic is fully closed: involves_human_subjects: true is matched by named IRB approval (University of South Florida, single-IRB for US subsites, separate Canadian REB approvals), by a detailed informed_consent block with a withdrawal mechanism, by at_risk_populations protections and by itemised participant_compensation.

Access restrictiveness is consistent across independent blocks: confidentiality_level restricted, a registered-access licence for features, a controlled-access DACO route for audio, a Certificate of Confidentiality, and a consent_scope that anticipates exactly this two-tier dissemination model.

Errata and anomalies cross-corroborate rather than duplicate: the anomaly recording broken Parquet files in v3.0.0 is matched by the v3.1.0 erratum fixing them, and the differing per-feature record counts are explained in both instances.notes and missing_data_documentation.

conforms_to carries an unusually precise scope caveat, stating that BIDS v1.9.0 applies to the audio layout and phenotype organisation rather than to the Parquet feature files of this release; this avoids a standards-conformance overclaim that the format list would otherwise imply.

Bias documentation uses the controlled BiasTypeEnum vocabulary (selection, representation, measurement, annotation) and each entry carries a causal account, with affected_subsets and mitigation_strategy where applicable, rather than a generic acknowledgement that bias may exist.

Processing software is named with a pinned version and repository (b2aiprep v3.0.0 at github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, senselab), and the feature-producing toolchain (torchaudio, openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, sparc, ppgs) is traceable from individual variables through measurement_technique.

sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,500 characters) covering 833 adult participants, five North American sites, the five condition cohorts, the tablet-administered acoustic protocol, the derived feature inventory (spectrograms, mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch contours, SPARC articulatory traces, phonetic posteriorgrams) as Parquet, the phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, and the withholding of raw recordings

The final sentence pre-empts the most consequential misreading by stating that original recordings are withheld and controlled-access only.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content matches the claimed dataset type throughout: acoustic-feature terminology is used correctly, and the participant count agrees with instances.counts and with the cumulative release additions in collection_timeframes.

sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License. Only credentialed PhysioNet users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement may access the files... Duplication as reasonably required to carry out the research project is permitted, but sale of all or part of the data on any media is not... respect the Fort Lauderdale Agreement. The IP block is unusually precise in distinguishing claims on the data itself, which are barred, from downstream discovery rights, which are permitted under non-obstructive licensing.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Restrictiveness is coherent with the surrounding record: general_research_use with no non-commercial or geographic limit matches collection_consents, which states the consent imposes no such restrictions. The licence and the consent scope agree.

A user can act on this without further enquiry.

sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on evidence outside this sub-element: distribution_formats is populated with three format entries and named files; page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; third_party_sharing.is_shared: true states the dataset is distributed broadly to individuals outside the creating entity.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms (Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, duplication for the research project permitted, sale barred, Fort Lauderdale Agreement respected, no fees); data_use_permission: general_research_use; prohibited_uses enumerating five specific bars

The absence of non-commercial, geographic, research-type or algorithm-development restrictions is affirmatively stated in collection_consents, which is what a prospective reuser needs to know.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: This is a bespoke registered-access licence rather than a standard Creative Commons instrument, so reuse terms must be read from the prose; the prose is specific enough to act on. Licence restrictiveness is consistent with the consent scope and with confidentiality_level: restricted.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, PhysioNet landing page for v3.1.0, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: Apache Parquet, Tab-separated values, JSON; conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0, applied to the audio dataset layout and the phenotype folder organization'; raw_data_sources.raw_data_format: 'WAV audio, converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz... REDCap and ReproSchema exports converted to tab-delimited phenotype tables'
sub_elements.quality_note: Every distributed product is in an open, widely supported, non-proprietary format, and each JSON data dictionary describes the columns, the question asked of the participant and the response type, which is what makes the TSV tables actually interpretable rather than merely machine-readable.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Formats are standard and correctly matched to content. Character encoding is nowhere stated for the TSV and JSON products; recorded as a low-severity completeness issue and counted as a warning rather than scored against the sub-element, since the dominant requirement — standardized, openly parseable formats — is met with file-level specificity.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible PhysioNet landing page, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0 with an explicit scope caveat; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology codes B2AI_TOPIC:4, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes'
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at three distinct levels — a community data-organisation standard (BIDS), a metadata schema (data-sheets-schema with a named class), and controlled vocabularies for topics, substrates and diagnoses (B2AI ontology codes, ICD-10). The scope caveat on BIDS is the mark of a careful claim rather than a weaker one.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The caveat that BIDS applies to the audio layout and phenotype folders and not to the Parquet feature files of this release is semantically correct and prevents a conformance overclaim that the format list would otherwise invite. Ontology prefixes are used consistently with the Bridge2AI namespace.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible PhysioNet landing page, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: thirteen entries. participant_id and session_id carry data_type: identifier with is_identifier: true and notes describing the linkage ('links feature records to phenotype rows'; 'a participant may have more than one session'). Feature variables carry derivation (e.g. spectrogram: 'STFT of the 16 kHz monaural waveform with a 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point FFT, downsampled by a factor of two; dimension 201 by T'), measurement_technique, unit, minimum_value/maximum_value (sparc_pitch 50–550 Hz) and quality_notes on absence
sub_elements.quality_note: Identifier variables are flagged as such and their join semantics explained, which is precisely what cross-dataset integration requires. Feature variables carry reproducible derivation parameters and dimensionality, and several record why a value may be absent. source_caveats honestly states that these are the shared identifying and dense-feature columns rather than a complete column enumeration, with the JSON dictionaries carrying the remainder.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Variable-level parameters agree with preprocessing_strategies (25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 mel bins, 50 Hz SPARC, 100 Hz ppgs across 40 phonemes) with no contradiction between the two blocks. The distinction drawn between torchaudio pitch and sparc_pitch as different algorithms over different ranges is technically coherent.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three research entries with examples and usage_notes ('No recommended splits are supplied; researchers should construct their own and should account for the skews in disorder category, site and demographics'); discouraged_uses: two entries (hiring, insurance, surveillance; uses assuming representativeness); prohibited_uses: five entries (re-identification attempts, harm or stigmatization, obstructive IP protection and sale, contacting subjects without IRB and consent, onward disclosure to third parties)
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated and each carries a reason rather than a bare prohibition. The three-way distinction is used correctly: legally binding bars sit in prohibited_uses, ethical cautions in discouraged_uses, and affirmative research applications in intended_uses. The usage note attaching split construction guidance to the intended use is the kind of guidance that changes what a reuser actually does.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibitions are consistent with the licence terms and the Registered Access Agreement described in license_and_use_terms, and the discouraged surveillance and insurance uses align with the stated ethical rationale for controlled access to raw voice.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 and E8 evidence, independent of this element's own fields: description states '833 adult participants recruited at five sites in North America' who 'completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks' and 'consented to clinician review of their records'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes a tablet application collecting acoustic tasks and questionnaires from participants, and data_collectors describes research teams conducting collection sessions. The governance condition is independently met: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (E2) is 'restricted' and other_compliance asserts a Certificate of Confidentiality.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: reviewing_organization 'University of South Florida Institutional Review Board' with review_details ('Reviewed and approved the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol and the sharing of the collected data. Subsites were approved through the single IRB process. The study is observational... no data monitoring committee was appointed'); human_subject_research.irb_approval ('Participating United States institutions were covered through the single IRB process; Canadian institutions obtained separate research ethics board approvals'); human_subject_research.ethics_review_board; data_protection_impacts; data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with DACO@b2ai-voice.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics oversight is documented with the reviewing body named, the multi-jurisdictional structure explained (single IRB for US subsites, separate Canadian REBs, a further separate protocol for genomic collection), the study design characterised, and the absence of a data monitoring committee justified by the observational design. The governance contact required by the source-rubric scope is present. The data protection impact limb is weaker: the record states that no impact analysis on data subjects has been conducted, offsetting this with an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published ethical-justification memorandum.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects: true is matched by populated IRB approval, as required. The consistency rule 'IF data_protection_impacts present THEN EXPECT reidentification_risk assessed' also passes — participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is assessed in detail. Scored 1 on the strength of the ethics-review limb, which is the sub-element's primary requirement; the missing DPIA is logged as a medium-severity content_accuracy issue.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1/E8 evidence as above (description names 833 adult participants and clinical cohorts; collection_mechanisms describes participant recruitment and collection sessions). Governance condition independently met via E2 confidentiality_level 'restricted' and the Certificate of Confidentiality in other_compliance.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, removal of selected indirect identifiers and highly sensitive non-identifying elements, and withholding of all raw audio'; identifiers_removed enumerating names, civic addresses, SSNs, geography above country, dates finer than years, contact and device identifiers, biometric identifiers, narrative free-text and transcripts, and all raw voice recordings; deidentification_details: 'Dates were rebased or replaced by integers, geographic information was generalized... K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved, and voice itself can never be fully de-identified, which is why the waveforms are released only under controlled access'
sub_elements.quality_note: Among the strongest sections of the record. A named standard, an enumerated identifier list, the specific transformations applied, and — unusually — a statement of what the method does not achieve. Declaring that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not reached, and tying that residual risk to the decision to withhold waveforms, is the sort of disclosure that lets a reuser reason about risk rather than take reassurance on trust.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method appropriateness check passes emphatically: HIPAA Safe Harbor alone would be inadequate for voice data, and the record recognises this, layering indirect-identifier removal, free-speech feature exclusion and complete withholding of raw audio on top. Consistency rules 'deidentification claimed THEN method specified' and 'identifiers removed THEN identifiers_removed listed' both pass.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1/E8 evidence: description references 833 adult participants, patients across clinical cohorts and clinician validation of diagnoses; collection_mechanisms and data_collectors (E8) describe participant recruitment and in-clinic collection sessions. Participants exist, so the sub-element's subject matter exists and it is scored rather than excluded.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers, indirect identifiers, state/province removed with only country retained, date rebasing, narrative removal, withholding of raw voice); privacy_techniques ('a combined de-identified database hosted through a HIPAA-compliant NIH STRIDES partner, and federated learning, in which algorithms are run on data held at each institution and only model updates are shared'); reidentification_risk ('Voice is inherently identifying... K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved... users agree not to attempt re-identification'); data_linkage describing EHR access for gold-standard validation and datasheets kept only at the collecting institution
sub_elements.quality_note: Re-identification risk is assessed explicitly and honestly rather than asserted away, and the assessment drives a concrete mitigation (controlled access for waveforms) rather than ending in a disclaimer. The architectural protections — federated learning so data need not leave institutions, identifiable PHI confined to institution-local REDCap — are described at a level that lets a reader evaluate them.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The risk assessment is technically correct about the data type: a voice waveform is a biometric and cannot be de-identified, and the record reaches the right conclusion from that premise. Consistent with is_deidentified.deidentification_details, which makes the same k-anonymity statement without contradiction.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: four entries using the BiasTypeEnum vocabulary — selection_bias (recruitment at high-volume expert clinics; 'Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in artificial intelligence, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, were less likely to be recruited', with a shift to remote collection as mitigation_strategy); representation_bias (unequal disease distribution, skew by site and demographics, with affected_subsets and mitigation); measurement_bias (site-specific devices and configurations, variable headset distance, noise artifacts, with affected_subsets); annotation_bias (single clinician, EHR or prescription-derived labels, varying diagnostic practice). future_use_impacts: three entries on generalization and unfair treatment, unaudited transcription models, and anticipated distribution shift
sub_elements.quality_note: Bias categories come from the controlled taxonomy and each carries a causal mechanism rather than an acknowledgement, with affected_subsets and mitigation_strategy where they apply. The selection_bias entry reaches beyond geography to trust in medicine and in AI, which is a substantive fairness analysis. The social-impact limb required by the source-rubric scope is covered by future_use_impacts.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Taxonomy terms are applied correctly to their mechanisms: device heterogeneity is measurement bias, cohort imbalance is representation bias, single-labeler diagnosis is annotation bias. No miscategorisation. Consistent with sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and with the subpopulations distribution statements.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: five entries — differing site collection configurations and a protocol that changed during the study; 'Noise artifacts are present in the recordings; the head-mounted headset microphone could sit at slightly different distances from participant to participant'; varying diagnostic practice between sites and clinicians, and possibly inaccurate or under-reported questionnaire responses; recordings that could not produce particular features, so record counts differ between feature types; 'Some Parquet files distributed in version 3.0.0 were broken and were fixed in version 3.1.0'
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies span acquisition artifacts, protocol drift, label-practice variability, systematic feature absence and an outright file defect in a prior release. Disclosing the broken Parquet files rather than quietly fixing them is a meaningful act of transparency toward anyone who analysed v3.0.0. The cleaning_strategies audit protocol and the released audio_quality_metrics.tsv give users the means to assess quality themselves.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The feature-absence anomaly is quantitatively corroborated by the differing per-feature counts in instances.notes and by variables.quality_notes; the Parquet defect is corroborated by the v3.1.0 erratum. Anomalies and known_biases overlap on device heterogeneity, which is appropriate since it is both a quality issue and a bias mechanism.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: content_warnings.content_warnings_present: true with warnings: 'The collection includes free speech tasks whose transcription may contain offensive or distressing content... Dense features and transcripts derived from free-speech prompts were removed from the released feature set, and audio recordings containing potentially identifying information or external voices were removed. Questionnaire content covers depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress and other psychiatric symptoms'; sensitive_elements: three entries (race and ethnic origin; sexual orientation; socioeconomic and health information including clinical diagnoses and psychiatric and respiratory questionnaire responses); confidential_elements with confidentiality_details
sub_elements.quality_note: Both limbs are populated and the warning is paired with the mitigation actually applied, so a user learns not only that free speech could contain distressing content but that the derived features and transcripts were removed on that account. The psychiatric questionnaire content is flagged, which matters for secondary analysts as well as for participants.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: A low-severity tension is logged between sensitive_elements_present: true for attributes such as sexual orientation and the notes on the same block stating that REDCap-flagged sensitive fields were removed before release; the scope of what survives into the published release is left ambiguous. This is a clarity defect rather than a contradiction, and the sub-element's requirement — that sensitive content be described and warnings given — is met.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: University of South Florida IRB with review_details covering the acquisition protocol, the sharing of collected data, single-IRB subsite approval, the observational design and the absence of a data monitoring committee; future_use_impacts: three entries — skew leading to poor generalization and potentially unfair treatment of groups; unaudited off-the-shelf transcription models whose errors may propagate downstream; anticipated distribution shift from changing site configurations, protocol and diagnostic practice. data_governance.notes cites the published memorandum 'Ethical Justification for Controlled Access to Raw Voice Data Samples'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both limbs are substantive. The social-impact analysis is forward-looking and specific about the mechanism of harm in each case, and the discouraged_uses entries on hiring, insurance and surveillance extend it to the misuse scenarios most plausible for voice biomarkers. A published ethics memorandum backs the governance design rather than leaving it asserted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: future_use_impacts correctly implements the rai:dataSocialImpact concept the source rubric points at. The ethical review is consistent with human_subject_research.irb_approval, which names the same board and the same single-IRB arrangement. Conflicts of interest are not addressed, which is a minor gap against the fullest reading of the scope but does not undercut the documented review.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, PhysioNet landing page for v3.1.0 accessible, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://physionet.org; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; maintainers[0]: 'PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and supported by NIBIB, NHLBI and the NIH Office of the Director, hosts the current releases and provides continued access to credentialed researchers'; maintainers[2] describes the Health Data Nexus (T-CAIREM, University of Toronto) which hosted v1.0
sub_elements.quality_note: PhysioNet is a recognised domain repository and the record goes further than naming it, identifying its operator, its funding support and its access model. The platform history including the earlier Health Data Nexus hosting is preserved rather than overwritten, so citations to v1.0 remain resolvable in context.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The publisher is consistent with the 10.13026 DOI prefix, which is PhysioNet's registrant prefix — platform identity is corroborated by the identifier rather than only asserted. source_caveats explains the preference for the PhysioNet statement over the project documentation's Health Data Nexus description.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Scored on the datasets-shared condition alone, as the instrument directs: distribution_formats populated, PhysioNet landing page accessible, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true. An existing publication is not a precondition for applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., Dorr, D., Payne, P., Ravitsky, V., Belisle-Pipon, J., Bahr, R., Watts, S., Bolser, D., Siu, J., Lerner-Ellis, J., Rudzicz, F., Boyer, M., Abdel-Aty, Y., Ahmed Syed, T., Anibal, J., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, formatted citation string with author list, year, versioned title, publisher and resolvable DOI — directly usable without reconstruction. Both the version-pinned and the version-independent DOI are available, so a citing author can choose whether to pin.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The citation's version (3.1.0), year (2026) and DOI all agree with the version, issued and doi fields. The embedded RRID:SCR_007345 is well formed but identifies PhysioNet rather than the dataset; logged as a low-severity semantic_understanding issue. Cross-referencing is fully served by the DOI.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible PhysioNet landing page, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0, applied to the audio dataset layout and the phenotype folder organization rather than to the Parquet feature files of the published feature-only release'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; external_resources includes 'FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, published by the consortium'; labeling uses ICD-10; instances use B2AI ontology codes
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance spans a community data-organisation standard with a version number, a metadata schema with a named class, a clinical interoperability standard (FHIR profiles the consortium itself contributed), and clinical and domain vocabularies. Contributing FHIR profiles back is community integration in the strong sense, not merely consumption of a standard.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The BIDS scope caveat is semantically precise and prevents an overclaim. The record candidly notes that the FHIR profile source repository URL is not captured in the bundle, distinguishing what it knows from what it does not.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible PhysioNet landing page, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: 'Project documentation and dashboards at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, with source code at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs' (MIT), plus the REDCap data dictionary and instrument PDFs at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived on Zenodo, b2aiprep and senselab repositories; page: the PhysioNet landing page; existing_uses: 'A restricted version of the dataset containing raw audio has been used in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon' and 'Training opportunities... through the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars program at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep
sub_elements.quality_note: Outreach is documented as an actual programme rather than a promise: a summer school, a hackathon and a named scholars programme with its own URL, alongside a documentation site with dashboards and openly licensed instrument PDFs. The extension mechanism invites contribution through repository issues and pull requests, which is a live community channel.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are well formed with plausible domains. The documentation, training and contribution routes are mutually consistent and consistent with the open-source licences declared on the same resources.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, accessible PhysioNet landing page, third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_supplemented_by doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric dataset v1.1.0, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2–18, Hospital for Sick Children REB, parental consent with child assent); is_new_version_of doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0); is_version_of doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI); is_new_version_of doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 (v1.0, Health Data Nexus); is_documented_by doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926; is_documented_by doi:10.5281/zenodo.12760724
sub_elements.quality_note: Six relationships, every one typed and DOI-resolvable, spanning a companion cohort, two prior versions, the concept identifier and two documenting works. Each carries a description substantial enough to tell a user whether the target is worth following, including the pediatric cohort's distinct ethics and assent arrangements.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are semantically correct throughout, with is_version_of reserved for the concept DOI and is_new_version_of for superseded releases. DOI prefixes are plausible for their targets: 10.13026 PhysioNet, 10.57764 Health Data Nexus, 10.21437 ISCA/Interspeech, 10.5281 Zenodo.

strengths: De-identification and re-identification risk are handled with rare intellectual honesty: the record names HIPAA Safe Harbor, enumerates the removed identifiers, states that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved, concedes that a voice waveform can never be fully de-identified, and lets that conclusion drive the actual design decision to withhold all raw audio behind controlled access.

Human-subjects documentation closes every loop the instrument checks: involves_human_subjects: true is matched by a named IRB with its multi-jurisdictional structure explained, a consent block covering type, documentation, scope and withdrawal, at-risk population protections, and itemised compensation with its cap.

The processing pipeline is specified to reimplementation standard — window, hop, FFT size, mel bins, frame rates and dimensionality for each feature family — and the per-variable derivation strings agree exactly with the preprocessing narrative, with the producing software named and pinned (b2aiprep v3.0.0) and its repository and licence given.

Internal arithmetic and chronology reconcile across independent blocks: 306 + 136 + 391 = 833 participants, the issued date matches the v3.1.0 release date, the landing page path matches the version field, and the broken-Parquet anomaly is matched by the corresponding erratum.

Limitations, biases and anomalies are disclosed against a controlled taxonomy with causal mechanisms rather than hedges, including uncomfortable admissions — a single labeler per diagnosis, psychiatric labels taken from prescriptions, unaudited Whisper transcriptions, and file defects shipped in a prior release.

source_caveats records where the underlying sources disagreed and which was preferred and why, so a reader can audit the record's own construction rather than having to trust it — including the 10,000 versus 30,000 enrollment conflict and the Health Data Nexus versus PhysioNet hosting question.
weaknesses: Keywords are the single scored failure: four broad terms that omit every disease cohort, acoustic feature family and modality the record documents elsewhere, leaving the dataset effectively undiscoverable by the searches most likely to want it.

No data protection impact assessment has been conducted, which sits awkwardly beside the record's own acknowledgement that voice is inherently identifying and that k-anonymity is not achieved; the ethicist field review and published memorandum are offered in its place.

Machine-readable distribution detail is thin relative to the prose: no download_url, no media_type on any format, no character encoding for the TSV and JSON products, and is_tabular unset despite tabular products being distributed.

The boundary between sensitive attributes retained in the published release and those removed during de-identification is left ambiguous, with sensitive_elements asserting presence and its own notes describing removal.

Several concepts are documented only in prose or in adjacent slots rather than in their dedicated structured fields — imputation in missing_data_documentation rather than imputation_protocols, the governance contact inside access_review_process — which is adequate for a human reader but weaker for automated consumption.
recommendations: Expand keywords to at least a dozen terms drawn from content the record already contains: the five disease cohorts, the acoustic feature families (spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram, articulatory coding), the modalities (speech, cough, breathing), and the platform and standards terms (PhysioNet, BIDS, FHIR).

Conduct and record a formal data protection impact assessment for the feature-only release, or state explicitly in data_protection_impacts why the published ethical-justification memorandum and ethicist field review are held to discharge that function.

Populate download_url with the PhysioNet v3.1.0 files endpoint, add media_type to each distribution_formats entry, state UTF-8 encoding for the text products, and set is_tabular to reflect the mixed tabular and array composition.
Scope each sensitive_elements entry to the release it describes, so a reader can tell which sensitive attributes survive into the published feature set and which were removed before release.

Move concepts documented in prose into their dedicated structured slots — a no-imputation imputation_protocols entry, data_governance.committee_contact for the DACO address — and label the PhysioNet RRID in the citation as a platform resource identifier rather than a dataset identifier.
